solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Famous actor, perhaps, one disembarking from flight

indicators.note: someone disembarking gets off, so that item leaves the word that follows

parts.note: a flight of steps is a stair
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A celebrity is spotted stepping off an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests an aeroplane, but it is a flight of stairs; take the I out of STAIR to leave STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a celebrated performer, and a famous actor is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Bowled over a scoundrel snatching one item of jewellery

indicators.note: something bowled over is knocked onto its back, so the following words are turned round
to snatch something is to grab and hold it, so one piece is clutched inside another

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed by a villain who steals a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' reads as amazed, but it turns A RAT round to TARA, which then takes in I after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headband or small crown, a piece of ornamental jewellery.

clue.text: A story he made up for Scottish island town

indicators.note: a made-up story is invented, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone invents a tale about a little Scottish town on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Rothesay is the main town on the Isle of Bute in the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Rothesay is the chief town of Bute, an island off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: US city last up for rebuilding

indicators.note: something up for rebuilding will be taken apart and put together differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American city is the most recent one due for redevelopment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' sits inside the surface phrase 'up for rebuilding' but belongs to the letters being shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul is the state capital of Minnesota, a city in the United States.

clue.text: Writer going round street to find restaurant

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writer
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An author strolls about the streets looking for somewhere to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is a pen: BIRO is the British brand name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant, originally French.

clue.text: Excited, I start to gambol between rugby posts

indicators.note: something placed between two things is enclosed by them on either side

parts.note: rugby goalposts are shaped like the letter H; the first of the pair
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of gambol
the second H-shaped post

explanation.surface: A rugby fan, thrilled, starts skipping about between the goalposts.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby posts form an H, and two of them, one each side, enclose I and G.
explanation.definitionFit: High can mean elated or excitable, in a state of heightened excitement.

clue.text: I note chin twitching in delicate situation

indicators.note: twitching is jerky, restless movement, so these letters jump into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone observes a nervous twitch in their chin during an awkward moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on thin ice is an idiom for being in a risky or precarious position.

clue.text: Beethoven symphony lifted heart around island area

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word lifted is read from bottom to top, so it runs backwards
one piece placed around another encloses it

parts.note: the heart of something is its core
I is the abbreviation for island
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A Beethoven symphony raised the spirits of everyone on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: CORE turned upward gives EROC, which wraps round I; A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony, named for its heroic character.

clue.text: Part of ship's company avoiding lucky charm

indicators.note: something avoiding a thing keeps clear of it, so that piece is left out

parts.note: a mascot is a lucky charm
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Some of a ship's crew steer clear of a superstitious token.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship's company' reads as the crew, but the definition stops at 'ship' and the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mast is the tall upright pole on a ship that carries the sails or rigging.

clue.text: Man with skill beat object of infatuation

parts.note: a man is a he
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
a throb is a beat, as of the heart

explanation.surface: A skilful man defeats someone he is besotted with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins HE to ART; 'beat' looks like a verb meaning defeat but is the noun THROB.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-throb is someone, usually a celebrity, whom people find intensely attractive and fall for.

clue.text: Unexciting, but not entirely blameable

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the next word is used, a run of its letters

parts.note: letters two to five of this word

explanation.surface: Something dull, though not wholly someone's fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame excuse or joke is weak and uninspiring, so lame means feeble or unexciting.

clue.text: First-class area on ship: ascend, look all over the place

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A passenger is told to go up to the posh part of the liner and look around everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The saloon deck on a passenger ship is the one reserved for first-class (saloon) passengers.

clue.text: Former award for winning? Not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a gold medal is the award for winning

explanation.surface: A question about a past prize for a victory, which was not first place.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the G from GOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Old can mean former or previous, as in 'my old school'.

clue.text: Very still warm weather? It's not a clear outcome

definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsical: heat with no movement in the air at all
second meaning: a race finish with no single winner

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first meaning is a playful reading of the words rather than a real term.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race in which two or more competitors finish level, so there is no outright winner.

clue.text: Nothing in this to assist in cleaner operation

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase: the thing with nothing in it
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a space entirely empty of matter

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase: the thing that helps a cleaner work
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the suction that drives a household cleaning machine

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are descriptions rather than synonyms: a space with nothing in it, and what makes a household cleaner suck up dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum is a space devoid of matter, and the low pressure it creates powers a vacuum cleaner.

clue.text: Some say she barely managed to change her husband's mind

definitions.text: Some say she barely managed to change her husband's mind

parts.words: Some say she barely managed to change her husband's mind
parts.note: surface reading: a wife who only just succeeded in persuading her husband
setter's reading: barely means naked, the legendary woman who rode unclothed through Coventry to make her husband cut taxes

explanation.surface: A wife who, according to legend, only just won an argument with her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says an 11th-century noblewoman rode naked through Coventry so her husband, Leofric, would lift a harsh tax; 'some say' nods to the story being legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Coventry noblewoman famously rode unclothed to persuade her husband to ease taxes.

clue.text: Unexpected error over variable astronomical model

indicators.note: something unexpected turns out differently, so these letters come out in another order

parts.note: taken as written
in algebra, x, y and z stand for variables

explanation.surface: A surprise mistake affects a changeable model of the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' places the shuffled letters above Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system showing the planets' movements.

clue.text: Start of month: turned up North American lizard

indicators.note: in a down entry, something turned up is flipped to read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: the first of August, written Aug 1 with a Roman numeral
N is the abbreviation for North
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: At the beginning of the month a North American lizard emerged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of month' is not a first letter: it is a date, 1 August, written AUG I.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard.

clue.text: Love: a term of endearment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: nil, as a score; in cricket a batter out for nought makes a ...
second meaning: a friendly address, as in 'all right

explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' looks like the endearment, but it is the zero score; 'duck' is a regional British way of addressing someone fondly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both love and duck mean zero in sport, and duck is also an affectionate form of address in parts of England.

clue.text: What doctor seeks, buttonholing one famous scientist

indicators.note: to buttonhole someone is to grab and detain them, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a doctor aims for a cure
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctor in pursuit of answers corners an eminent scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Curie, pioneer of radioactivity research, won Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry.

clue.text: Rehearse attack with sword?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: practise a performance from start to finish
second meaning: pierce someone with a blade

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark suggests an actor rehearsing a sword fight, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To run through a play is to rehearse it, and to run someone through is to stab them with a sword.

clue.text: What's signified by tense in sentence?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: grammatical tense marks when an action happens

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about grammar, tense inside a sentence; but 'sentence' is a separate meaning, a spell in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb tense indicates time, and a prisoner serving a sentence is said to be doing time.

clue.text: Merit retained by nuclear nations

indicators.note: something retained by other words is kept inside them, held within their letters

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Some value is kept by countries with nuclear weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve it, as you earn praise by your actions.

clue.text: Bloke going round city returned with US lawyer to make notes

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a bloke is a man

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Italian capital city
a DA is a District Attorney, a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A man tours a city and comes back with an American lawyer to jot things down.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is the one read backwards, and 'going round' makes the bloke enclose it; DA is the standard abbreviation for a US prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda, plural of memorandum, are written notes or reminders.

clue.text: Long journey ends in disappointment for the monk

indicators.note: ends in the following words means only the closing letter of each is kept

parts.note: the final letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A long walk finishes with disappointment for a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ends in disappointment' reads as a result, but 'ends' picks the last letter of each word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, arduous journey, usually on foot.
